A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same safety-alignment framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments on Llama2 and Qwen2.5, plus reward-model analyses, ablations and additional evaluations in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds SimPO comparison results and a toxic-policy robustness experiment.

M1.justification: Section 5.5 adds a two-stage adaptation for severely misaligned policies: safety SFT followed by the existing alignment procedure. The layerwise probes, reward aggregation, preference-confidence objective and per-batch updates remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds reverse-alignment training on Real-Toxicity-Chat and evaluates subsequent alignment of an intentionally toxic policy. This extends coverage to recovery from severe initial misalignment; the existing main and appendix benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds a SimPO baseline while retaining the previous comparators. Although Section 4.5 mentions integrating SimPO with the hybrid reward, no SimPO+HR result is reported.

E3.justification: The reported confidence scale changes from alpha = 7.5 in v1 Appendix F to alpha = 1 in v2 Appendix E; beta, learning rate and batch size remain unchanged. v2 also introduces the reverse-alignment and SFT-control protocol for Table 3. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new Section 5.5/Table 3 tests robustness when alignment requires a large policy shift and contrasts toxic-policy and SFT initialization. Existing analyses remain, including the reward-strategy analysis moved from v1 Section 5.4 to v2 Appendix E.1.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds or significance tests. The existing shaded regions in the convergence plots are retained without additional statistical explanation.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 values and matched appendix results are retained. v2 adds SimPO's 28.2% average toxicity in Table 2 and toxic-policy results of 48.2% before versus 44.1% after cDPO in Table 3. That table's SFT results, 28.0% and 21.4%, repeat existing Table 1 values.

T1.justification: The EBM derivation moves from v1 Appendix C to v2 Section 5.2 without substantive mathematical revision. However, the sampling-cost derivation replaces (512 - 128) with 386 in v2 Equation 19, an incorrect, non-equivalent substitution; the stated 256-times-forward estimate remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the claim from 'effectively eliminates' distribution shift to 'alleviates' it. The central hypothesis, representation-based reward contribution, safety-improvement claims and approximately 300-fold computational savings remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 adds a specific applicability boundary: large unsafe-to-safe shifts weaken the underlying hypothesis. It attributes weak improvement to predominantly negative top-k rewards that obscure useful ranking information and recommends initial safety SFT. These qualifications supplement the retained limitations.

D1.justification: v1 promises code and data release upon acceptance; v2 states they are available and supplies a repository link. The parameter appendix also changes the reported confidence scale from 7.5 to 1 without explaining the revision.

R1.justification: v2 adds Meng et al. (2024) on SimPO and briefly positions it as a reference-free comparison method. The existing related-work discussion and other matched references are retained.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and selected methodological and experimental explanations, separates settings from baselines, and adds acknowledgments. It moves the derivation into Section 5.2 and the reward-strategy analysis into Appendix E.1, while retaining the overall organization and much of the prose.

P2.justification: v2 substantially revises presentation: Figure 1 is replaced, Figure 4 is relabeled, Table 1 is regrouped by backbone, and a robustness table is added. Figures are relocated, appendix prose changes from one column to two, the 13B PCA display is substantially reduced, and the case-study tables share one page.

improvement.justification: The new robustness experiment provides useful evidence about where the central hypothesis fails, while SimPO broadens comparison and revised explanations and access information improve usability. These are limited gains because most results remain unchanged. The unexplained alpha revision, incorrect 386 substitution and smaller appendix plots temper the improvement.
